content:
- Overestimate prices when sentiment is positive and recent highs are followed by a spike — model tends to overshoot after bullish sentiment peaks.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative or shows strong downward momentum — model fails to recognize bearish sentiment’s drag on prices.
- Model consistently overreacts to short-term sentiment swings, especially when sentiment drops sharply — forecasts lag behind true price corrections.
- When sentiment is neutral or mildly positive, model often assumes continuation of trend and overestimates — true price tends to mean-revert toward prior range.
- In cases of strong upward momentum, model forecasts peak too early and then drops sharply — true price often holds or recovers slightly after model’s “peak”.
- Model underestimates prices during prolonged negative sentiment — fails to account for sentiment-driven volatility suppression.
- When sentiment is high but recent price action is flat, model tends to overproject upward — true price often stalls or reverses.
- Model exhibits bias toward higher prices in early forecast horizon (e.g., 1–3 days) when sentiment is bullish — true price often corrects within 5–7 days.
- Sentiment-driven volatility is under-predicted in model — true price swings are more frequent and sharper than forecasted, especially when sentiment is volatile.
